newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yaohan says to scale back overseas operations.
newsitem.headline: Yaohan says to scale back overseas operations.

text.p: Yaohan Japan said on Monday that the Yaohan retailing group would slim down its overseas operations as part of restructuring measures.
Yaohan Japan, the group's flagship firm, said in a statement the group plans to close down a store in Singapore next June and sell shares in its Malaysian subsidiary.
The firm also plans to close its second store in Thailand and reopen the facilities as a retail complex for wholesalers.
The restructuring also includes moves to postpone or freeze plans to open new stores in Japan, and to cut down the number of board members to 10 from the current 17.
Under its austerity plan, the company will cut the salaries of its chairman and president by 50 percent beginning from this month, the statement said.
Similarly, the salaries of its three vice presidents will be cut by 30 percent and its directors will have their pay cut by 15 percent, the statement said.
Executive bonuses for the board members will also be halted, the statement said.
The restructuring plan also includes slimming down the company's total assets and reducing its debts.
The statement said the redemption of its warrant bonds on December 10 was completed with the help of Daiwa Bank Ltd and other banks.
It also said that Yaohan Japan's suppliers had agreed to its request to extend the time-lag between merchandise delivery and payment to two months from the current one month.
The company said last week that it has asked its wholesalers and other suppliers to accept the longer delay.
